title: Advisory committee redesign and governance review
subtitle: Also: property tax ratios, single-use reusable containers, Vision Zero action plan, and a referred social media code of conduct.
overview: The Committee of the Whole recommended a redesign of the City's advisory committees, replacing the current 14 with seven new ones and dissolving the older groups once new members are appointed. It added broader membership skills for two committees {{vote:m5}}, but a change widening the Heritage Advisory Committee's membership failed {{vote:m6}}. The full package was recommended {{vote:m7}}.

On the 2025 governance review, the committee referred the proposed Code of Conduct, including its social media rules, back to staff to address councillors' concerns {{vote:m9}}. A proposal to give the Accessibility Advisory Committee input into appointments, and to pause its recruitment, was defeated {{vote:m10}}. The rest of the review, including the Procedure By-law and a new pregnancy and parental leave policy, was recommended {{vote:m11}}.

The committee also recommended the 2025 property tax ratios and rates {{vote:m2}}, a reusable-container requirement for food businesses with exemptions {{vote:m15}}, and the Vision Zero action plan with a new Community Safety Zone Policy {{vote:m16}}. After the closed session, the Mayor reported that Council received an update on a 601 Scottsdale Drive Ontario Land Tribunal matter and gave staff direction. The Mayor also gave an update on tariff-related procurement work. All recommendations go to Council for final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the 2025 property tax ratios and corresponding tax rates.
The committee recommended approving terms of reference for seven new advisory committees, new meeting and appointment policies, and dissolving the older committees once new members are appointed.
The committee recommended adding wider expertise areas to the membership of the Economic Development and Tourism Advisory Committee and the Committee of Adjustment and Property Standards Committee.
The committee referred the proposed Code of Conduct for Council and Local Boards back to staff to address concerns raised by councillors.

The committee recommended approving the Procedure By-law, the pregnancy and parental leave policy, the electronic-publication change to the Public Notice Provisions Policy, and Delegation of Authority By-law amendments.

The committee recommended requiring food businesses to accept customers' clean reusable containers or provide their own reusable ones, with exemptions for self-serve restaurants and businesses with a written reusable-container policy.
The committee recommended approving the Vision Zero action plan and a Community Safety Zone Policy effective July 1, 2025, and directed staff to bring forward a revised Traffic By-law.

debate: On the Heritage Advisory Committee, the councillor who moved the change argued that wider expertise such as education, community engagement and heritage organizations would draw more nominees. Planning staff said it was unclear how education and community engagement relate to heritage planning expertise, and noted the Heritage Act is prescriptive. The change failed on a tie.

On the Code of Conduct, councillors said the social media rules were unclear and possibly unworkable. They raised concerns about limits on using the title "councillor", blocking users, posting about events, local board members' personal accounts, and free expression. They also noted that candidates who are not sitting members would not be covered. The integrity commissioner said the rules draw on Toronto's code and are complaint-based. The Clerk recommended referral rather than rewriting on the spot.

On accessibility committee input into appointments, delegates and the committee chair argued that people with lived experience can spot gaps and concerns staff may miss. Councillors who opposed the amendment raised concerns about closed-session appointment decisions and wanted the matter handled separately. The mover said a confidential process could work without prescribing details.

On reusable containers, a restaurant industry delegate said accepting customer containers raises food safety, cost and space concerns at a time of financial strain. Staff said public health had been consulted, many businesses already accept containers, and the by-law would not override food safety rules. Councillors supported the staff amendment as a compromise and asked for annual reporting on results.

On Vision Zero, delegates supported the plan and described their own experiences of collisions. Councillors asked about arterial roads, speed camera operations and revenue, how high-risk roads were selected, and tracking progress. Staff said there are no direct financial implications and committed to follow-up on several questions.
